newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan saw 12 new kerosene importers in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Japan saw 12 new kerosene importers in 1996/97.

text.p: Japan's deregulation of oil product imports last April drew 12 new companies into the kerosene import business in fiscal 1996/97, an official for the Agency of Natural Resources and Energy said on Friday.
In addition, three firms were newly registered at the agency as gasoline importers and four companies as gas oil importers in fiscal 1996/97, which ended on March 31.
Some firms registered as an importer of more than one oil product, the official said.
He added that most of the new importers were trading houses, although their names were not disclosed.
Prior to last April's liberalisation, the importing of gasoline, kerosene and gas oil was almost entirely limited to domestic refiners.

Traders said oil products imported by the new participants in 1996/97 were expected to account for less than one percent of total Japanese demand, as imported cargoes were not competitive in the domestic market due to the weaker yen.

Earlier this week, trading house Itochu Corp, one of the three firms newly registered as gasoline importers, said it had no intention of importing gasoline for the time being due to the yen's depreciation.
